Leakage guardThis report is descriptive. Associations with the outcome - odds ratios, AUROCs, Table 1 - are shown for understanding only. No predictor is added, dropped or re-binned because of them; the predictor list and the bins are fixed in src/ctg/config.py before any of this was run. Choosing variables by their association with the outcome on the whole dataset would leak test-fold information into every model trained later. The single exception the plan allows is removing a redundant predictor (Section E), because redundancy is measured between predictors and never looks at the outcome.
Data quality at a glance
  • No implausible values found in any variable → handled by Section C, which still writes the cleaned file so later milestones read one input.
  • No variable exceeds 20% missing → the prior has a nearly complete item set for every labour.
  • 4 model bins hold fewer than 5 adverse labours and 0 more are rare (<5% of labours) → handled by Laplace smoothing (alpha = 1), which pulls their likelihood ratios towards 1, and by reporting each item's fold-to-fold spread in the results report.
  • 3 predictor pair(s) exceed |rho| or V of 0.3 → handled by excluding gravidity (parity carries the same information), by the lambda shrinkage on the CTG evidence, and by measuring calibration rather than assuming it.
  • 1 outcome definitions have fewer than 40 events (Apgar5 < 7) → handled by using the composite definition as the headline and running the others only as sensitivity analyses, always printing n beside every percentage.
  • Signal loss is similar in adverse and normal labours (difference 1.8 percentage points) → dropping poor windows should not bias the evaluation.
  • Class imbalance is 3.9 : 1 (113 adverse of 552) → handled by never reporting accuracy, by tuning thresholds for sensitivity inside the folds, and by showing precision-recall and decision curves beside every ROC.

A. Outcomes: what the model is asked to predict

The outcome is a surrogate for fetal compromise: umbilical artery acidaemia and/or a low Apgar score at 5 minutes. Neither is the same as injury or NICU need, and the CTU-UHB authors report no severe neonatal morbidity in this cohort.

Outcome definitions: events, rates and class imbalance.

Sparse outcome definitionsThese definitions have fewer than 40 events: Apgar5 < 7. Few events means wide confidence intervals and unstable Naive Bayes likelihood tables, because several categories will contain almost no adverse labours and Laplace smoothing will dominate them. These definitions are used only as sensitivity analyses, never as the headline.
What this class balance means for the evaluationThe composite outcome occurs in 113 of 552 labours (20.5%), a ratio of about 3.9 normal to 1 adverse. With this imbalance, accuracy is misleading: a monitor that never alarms would already be 79.5% accurate and would catch nothing. So accuracy is not a target anywhere in this project. Evaluation uses sensitivity first, with specificity, precision-recall curves and decision curve analysis beside it; thresholds are tuned inside the cross-validation folds for high sensitivity (target 90%); and the Naive Bayes carries the imbalance explicitly in its prior log-odds rather than hiding it.

Sparse bins in the prior4 Naive Bayes bins hold fewer than 5 adverse labours: age_band=<20 (1.1 adverse), diabetes=1.0 (6.7 adverse), preeclampsia=1.0 (3.1 adverse), pyrexia=1.0 (1.1 adverse). Laplace smoothing (alpha = 1) will dominate their likelihood ratios, pulling them towards 1. That is the intended behaviour - a rare category should not swing the probability on the strength of two or three labours - but it means these items add almost nothing to the prior, and their fold-to-fold variation in the results report will look large.

C. Plausibility checks and cleaning

Statistical outliers that are clinically possible are kept: the model bins them anyway, and removing a genuine 42-year-old would be throwing away real signal. Only values that cannot be true are set to missing, and Naive Bayes simply skips a missing item.

The plausibility rules applied

Age14 to 55set to missing

Gravidity1 to 20set to missing
Parity0 to 15set to missing

binary flags0 or 1set to missing
Presentationcodes [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]unknown code set to missing
ParityParity <= GravidityParity set to missing
Deviation from the written cleaning rule: parity vs gravidityThe written rule for parity was Parity < Gravidity, on the usual reading that gravidity counts every pregnancy including the current one. In this release Parity > Gravidity never occurs (0 labours), while Parity == Gravidity occurs in 115 labours (21% of the cohort), overwhelmingly as Parity = 1 with Gravidity = 1. A violation that systematic is a coding convention - gravidity recorded as previous pregnancies - not 115 independent data-entry errors. Applying the rule as written would have set 115 parity values to missing and cost the nullipara item for a fifth of the cohort, all of them multiparous women. The rule is therefore applied as Parity > Gravidity, the only true impossibility, and the equality cases are kept. Gravidity is excluded from the model either way, so this affects only nullipara. Logged in decisions_log.md.

D. Missing data

Naive Bayes skips a missing item instead of imputing it, so a labour with no recorded pre-eclampsia status simply gets no contribution from that item. What matters here is whether missingness itself is informative.

How missing values are handled downstreamThe clinical Naive Bayes skips missing items: a labour with no recorded value for an item receives a contribution of exactly zero from it, and its probability is built from the items that are present. Nothing is imputed, so no artificial value is ever invented for a mother. The CTG side is different - a window feature that cannot be computed is filled with the training-fold median, which is fitted inside the fold and so carries no leakage.

E. Redundancy between predictors

Naive Bayes multiplies each item's likelihood ratio as if the items were independent given the outcome. Two items that say the same thing therefore get counted twice, and the probability becomes overconfident. This section measures how badly that assumption is violated.

ParityGraviditySpearman rho0.480only parity is used; gravidity is excluded
What this means for the prior3 pair(s) exceed the 0.3 threshold. Gravidity and parity are the known case, and the plan already handles it by using only parity. Redundancy is the one EDA finding allowed to remove a predictor, because it does not look at the outcome - but no other pair reaches the 0.6 level that would require dropping an item, so the predictor list stays exactly as fixed in config.py.

F. Risk-factor burden

Guidelines separate 'low risk' from 'high risk' labours by whether any recognised risk factor is present. This subgroup is reported again in the results, because a monitor that only works in already-flagged pregnancies adds little.

H. CTG signal overview

The model reads the trace as well as the history, so the demo needs one page on what the signal actually looks like. Aggregates only.

Does signal loss track the outcome?Median FHR signal loss is 20.2% in adverse labours versus 18.4% in normal ones. The two are close enough that signal loss looks unrelated to outcome, so dropping poor windows should not bias the evaluation.

Data quality at a glance

Every flag this EDA raised, each ending with what the pipeline does about it.

  • No implausible values found in any variable → handled by Section C, which still writes the cleaned file so later milestones read one input.
  • No variable exceeds 20% missing → the prior has a nearly complete item set for every labour.
  • 4 model bins hold fewer than 5 adverse labours and 0 more are rare (<5% of labours) → handled by Laplace smoothing (alpha = 1), which pulls their likelihood ratios towards 1, and by reporting each item's fold-to-fold spread in the results report.
  • 3 predictor pair(s) exceed |rho| or V of 0.3 → handled by excluding gravidity (parity carries the same information), by the lambda shrinkage on the CTG evidence, and by measuring calibration rather than assuming it.
  • 1 outcome definitions have fewer than 40 events (Apgar5 < 7) → handled by using the composite definition as the headline and running the others only as sensitivity analyses, always printing n beside every percentage.
  • Signal loss is similar in adverse and normal labours (difference 1.8 percentage points) → dropping poor windows should not bias the evaluation.
  • Class imbalance is 3.9 : 1 (113 adverse of 552) → handled by never reporting accuracy, by tuning thresholds for sensitivity inside the folds, and by showing precision-recall and decision curves beside every ROC.
